headline: Severe load shedding disrupts daily life, with rural areas facing power cuts for half the day
summary: Bangladesh is experiencing severe load shedding, particularly in rural areas where power is unavailable for up to half a day. This crisis is exacerbated by import dependence in the fuel sector and systemic issues.
details: Bangladesh is currently grappling with severe load shedding, significantly disrupting daily life across the nation. Rural areas are particularly hard-hit, experiencing power outages for up to half of each day.
The country's energy sector is struggling due to its heavy reliance on imports for fuel. This dependency makes the power supply vulnerable to global market fluctuations and supply chain disruptions.

Compounding the issue are reports of "ghost bills" and systemic inefficiencies within the power distribution network. These problems contribute to the overall instability and public dissatisfaction with electricity services.

The persistent power cuts impact various aspects of life, from household chores and education to small businesses and agricultural activities. Citizens face challenges in their daily routines and economic productivity.

headline: Houthis kill 4 crew in Red Sea attack; US fires missiles at cargo ship, Iran warns on Hormuz
summary: Escalating tensions in vital global oil chokepoints saw a US Navy helicopter fire missiles at a cargo ship, while a Houthi attack in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait resulted in four deaths. Iran has also threatened to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed.
details: The US and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis reported separate attacks on shipping on Tuesday, dimming prospects for ending the Iran war. Tehran also stated the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed unless Washington accepts its conditions.

A suspected Houthi attack on a small cargo vessel in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait killed four crew members on Tuesday. Two Yemeni rescuers from an anti-Houthi military group were also killed in the incident.

The fatalities aboard the Egyptian-owned Tihamah mark the first deaths on shipping by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis since the Iran war began. The Houthi-run news agency Saba claimed the group attacked a Saudi ship carrying military equipment.

Separately, the US military reported a US Navy MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles to disable the steering gear of a Panama-flagged cargo ship. The vessel reportedly ignored repeated warnings to stop violating a naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Maritime sources told Reuters that the US strike occurred off Pakistan while the ship was sailing into the Gulf of Oman. Both the Gulf of Oman and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait are vital chokepoints for global oil supplies.

Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, stated that the vital Strait of Hormuz shipping route will remain closed. This is contingent on the US accepting Iran's conditions, which include the release of frozen assets and an end to regional conflicts.

This follows a new demand from former US President Donald Trump that Iran should pay compensation for people killed in 50 years of wars, attacks, and protests. Trump has alternated between threats of escalation and claims of an imminent peace deal.

In an interview, Trump suggested the uncertainty could persist, indicating he might "bop along" and let Tehran fail economically, or hit them "really, really hard." He later asserted, "We totally control the Strait of Hormuz... Nobody else, only us."

Rezaei's comments are the strongest indication that the Strait of Hormuz, which handled a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas flow before the war, may not reopen to shipping anytime soon. There was no immediate comment from Washington.

Amid renewed pessimism about a quick end to the conflict, oil prices gained and global shares retreated. Brent crude futures climbed 1.4% to settle at $88.91 per barrel, and US crude rose 1.3% to $83.20.
